title: Question set
description: One question set: data/sets/<id>.json. The same shape is used inside a shared set file ({ "format": "study-buddy-set", "formatVersion": 1, "set": … }).

id.description: Stable id, the same as the file name. Attempt history refers to it, so it is never renamed or reused.

name.description: Name shown in the app, e.g. “U.S. citizenship civics test (2008 version)”.

module.description: The bigger subject this set is a chapter of, e.g. “Human anatomy”. Built-in sets with the same module are offered together, as its chapters, in data/sets.json order.

description.description: A sentence or two on what the set is for and how the real test works.

source.description: Where the questions and answers come from.

updated.description: Date the answers were last checked against the source (YYYY-MM-DD).

questions.description: The questions, in the order the source lists them.

tests.description: Practice tests suggested for this set. Starting a programme with the set adds these as its test types.

id.description: Stable id within the set. Attempt history refers to it, so it is never renamed or reused.

prompt.description: The question as it is asked.

answers.description: Every answer that counts as right. Words in (brackets) are optional when typing an answer. Left out for a personal question.

personal.description: Makes the answer the person’s own. The app asks them for it before they practise, and keeps it with their data, never in shared files.

ask.description: What to ask them for, e.g. “Your state’s Governor”.

hint.description: Where to find it, and what to answer in special cases.

need.description: How many of the answers you have to give, for questions like “Name two…”. Leave out for one.

wrong.description: Wrong answers to offer in multiple choice. Without them the app borrows answers from other questions in the set.

explanation.description: Shown with the answer: why it is right, or a way to remember it.

note.description: A caution shown with the answer, e.g. that it changes after an election.

figure.description: A picture shown with the question, such as a circuit diagram it asks about, or (with `reveal`) one shown with the answer. Record where an image comes from and its licence when it isn’t the app’s own.

src.description: The image: a path in this app (data/figures/<file>) or an https link.

alt.description: Text that stands in for the picture.

reveal.description: Show the picture only with the answer, because it gives the answer away (e.g. the bone a question names, highlighted).

credit.description: Who made the picture or what it is made from, shown under it, e.g. “BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science”.

source.description: Link to where the picture, or what it was made from, comes from.

license.description: The picture’s licence, e.g. “CC BY-SA 2.1 JP” or “Public domain”.

tags.description: Topics the question belongs to. Practice tests can be limited to some of them.

question.description: A question with its answers, or (with `personal`) one whose answer is different for everyone, such as your state’s capital: each person fills theirs in before practising.

name.description: Name shown on the test's card.

count.description: How many questions the test asks. 0 asks every question.

pass.description: Percent of the questions you need right to pass.

pick.description: Which questions it asks: random; weakest first (missed recently, then new, then least sure); due for review first (spaced repetition: missed ones, then ones whose review gap of 1, 3, 7, 16 or 35 days has passed); new ones first; only ones missed last time; or in the set's order.

answer.description: How you answer: flip the card and mark yourself; pick from multiple choice; or type the answer.

feedback.description: Show whether you were right after each question, or only at the end.

stopEarly.description: End the test as soon as you have passed, or can no longer pass, like the U.S. civics interview.

tags.description: Only ask questions with one of these tags. Empty or left out asks from all.

why.description: Why this test is set up the way it is, shown on its card.
